rows.name: Freeman, Dea. Dyer House

evidence.statement: - Massing and roof (from the update sheet - the best comparative description of a Webster house type anywhere in this range). "This is one of four similar generously sized Greek Revival/Italianate houses built on East Main Street in the 1840s and 50s, three of them in the Center Area. The type seems to have set the standard of the period for middle class building in Webster. A fifth house, the now expanded house at 2 Lincoln Street (MHC #172) probably had a somewhat different plan and was more ornate, having a recessed door and leaded sidelights. These four all rest on massive granite block foundations and rise two-and-one-half stories. The temple front houses have three bays on the facade, turn their gable ends to the street and have original rear extensions. Doors in the first bay suggest a side-hall plan. Three of these houses, like this one, have full pediments and continuous cornices, most, as here quite plain. Their paneled pilasters represent three-dimensional classical columns in more easily constructed and less expensive two dimensions. However, these houses are not identical as their details vary."
